newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Clinton, Jiang may exchange visits - U.S. officials.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Jiang may exchange visits - U.S. officials.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and Chinese President Jiang Zemin will probably agree to hold a high-level exchange of visits starting next year when they meet on the fringes of the Asia-Pacific trade summit, a senior U.S. official said on Sunday.
"It's likely that they will discuss and maybe announce high-level visits starting with Vice President (Al) Gore," the official told Reuters.
Another U.S. official told Reuters: "They will unfold a series of meetings in 1997 and 1998."
He said the expected scenario was a visit by Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen to Washington in February or March, followed by a visit by Vice President Gore to Beijing.
Chinese Premier Li Peng would then visit the United States followed by a summit in Washington in the second half of 1997 after Hong Kong is transferred to Chinese rule.

Clinton would be the first U.S. leader to visit the world's most populous country since George Bush in early 1989. Relations between Washington and Beijing then went into a tailspin following the Tiananmen Square clampdown on dissidents in June of that year.
